name: PRODUCT
description: PRODUCT multiplies all the numbers given as arguments or contained in the referenced ranges.

parameters.name: number1
parameters.description: The first number, range, or cell reference to multiply.

parameters.name: number2
parameters.description: Additional numbers, ranges, or references (optional). Up to 255 arguments.

advancedExamples.title: Multiply an entire range
advancedExamples.explanation: PRODUCT multiplies every numeric cell in the range; text and blanks are ignored.

advancedExamples.title: A zero anywhere zeroes the product
advancedExamples.description: Show the effect of a zero factor.
advancedExamples.explanation: Any factor of 0 makes the whole product 0.

howItWorks: PRODUCT multiplies all numeric values across its arguments. Empty cells, text, and logical values in ranges are ignored, but explicitly typed TRUE/FALSE and numbers are multiplied. Supplying zero yields zero.

howToSteps.name: Select the cell
howToSteps.text: Click the cell for the product.

limitations: Empty cells, text, and logical values inside ranges are ignored (unlike explicitly entered TRUE/FALSE).
A single zero factor makes the entire product zero.

commonErrors.cause: The product is too large to represent.
commonErrors.fix: Use logarithms (EXP(SUMPRODUCT(LN(range)))) or scale the inputs.

commonErrors.cause: A zero is present in the data.
commonErrors.fix: Inspect the range for zeros or use an array formula that excludes them.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: PRODUCT works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: Does PRODUCT ignore text and blanks?
faq.answer: Yes, within ranges text and empty cells are ignored, so they don't contribute a zero.

faq.question: How is PRODUCT different from multiplying with *?
faq.answer: PRODUCT can take ranges and many arguments at once and skips non-numeric cells, while * requires each operand explicitly.

faq.question: What happens with a zero in the range?
faq.answer: The entire product becomes 0, since multiplying by zero yields zero.
